Unapologetic Mercedes-Benz GT Design Project Was Done by an Intern; It's Ready for Cannonball 2030
12 photos
Photo: cardesignworld / Instagram
Just recently, Mercedes-Benz CEO Ola Kallenius confirmed at the Golden Steering Wheel awards in Berlin that his company will introduce a new SL version for 2027, separating the series into three distinct personalities.
There’s the initial AMG version as well as the ultra-luxurious Maybach, and soon there will be a comfort-focused model which probably reverts the nameplate to a Mercedes-Benz moniker. The company also has another type of vehicle at the top of the ‘sports car’ category – the all-new second-generation Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupé (C590), aka the sports brand’s first dedicated all-electric performance model.
It rides on the bespoke 800-volt AMG.EA architecture and was revealed earlier in 2026 with YASA-developed axial-flux electric motors and F1-derived battery technology, plus up to 1,169 hp for the top GT 63 4Matic+ model. It was swiftly followed by the GT SUV sibling, and both have been at the center of intense discussions about Mercedes’ new EV styling, which has been pretty controversial, to say the least.
But there are other ways to be unapologetic in terms of design and still make a positive impact on Mercedes-Benz fans: the good folks over at Car Design World (aka ' cardesignworld ' on social media) tipped us off to this official intern design project by artist Lukas Worsche, who recently completed a Mercedes Advanced Design Internship and wrapped up the stage with his own take on a Mercedes GT sports car.
The idea was pretty wacky, indeed: What if Mercedes developed a car specifically for the Cannonball Run? By the way, the Cannonball Run is a 1981 action-comedy film starring an all-star ensemble cast, including Burt Reynolds, Dom DeLuise, Roger Moore, Farrah Fawcett, Jackie Chan, Sammy Davis Jr., and Dean Martin, inspired by an actual cross-country outlaw road race – the 1979 running of the Cannonball Baker Sea-to-Shining-Sea Memorial Trophy Dash.
Today, the modern Cannonball Run is an unsanctioned speed record attempt that involves driving across the US, traditionally from New York City's Red Ball Garage to the Portofino Hotel in Redondo Beach, California, near Los Angeles, running a distance of about 2,813 miles (4,527 km). The current record was achieved in May 2020 during early Covid-19 lockdowns, but that doesn’t mean it was any less perilous because of the sustained high speeds.
Anyway, this Mercedes GT would be a purpose-built machine for the Cannonball Run, but other than that, its unapologetic design works extremely well for an alternate option to the GT 4-Door EV, as this coupe has the allure of a traditional grand tourer but also the muscle of an EV supercar. There are massive aerodynamic elements, muscly fenders, a small cabin, and a huge front hood, along with an extreme powertrain.
As far as we can tell, the artist chose ‘direction 2’ of the project, which apparently involves a hybrid powertrain using separate wheel hub electric motors at the rear along with two compact jet turbines for the front, one each in the oversized front fenders!
